script.title: Compound Interest and Effective Rate
script.caption_hook: Interest on interest? Here's how compound interest really grows your money.

lines.say: Interest on interest? How is that even a thing?
Each period, interest joins the principal. Next time, you earn interest on a bigger amount.
So money grows faster every period?
Take ₹10,000 at 10% per annum. Year one interest: ₹1,000. Year two: ten percent of ₹11,000.
Simple interest would give ₹1,000 again, right?
Right. So two-year compound interest is ₹2,100, simple is ₹2,000. Now the formula.

board.title: Amount formula
board.sub: r = % per year, n = years, m = times a year

lines.say: Compounding times per year. Same ₹10,000, 10% per annum, half-yearly, two years: m is 2.
Rate 5% per half-year, four half-yearly periods?
Yes! Rate divided by m, periods times m. A is ₹10,000 times 1.05 to the power 4.
And compound interest is amount minus principal?
Yes. Amount about ₹12,155.06 minus ₹10,000 gives CI of ₹2,155.06.
The yearly rate with the same growth: 1.05 squared minus 1, which is 10.25%.

board.title: Effective rate
board.sub: i = nominal rate (0.10), m = times a year

lines.say: Remember: rate divided by m, periods times m. More compounding means higher effective rate.

check_notes: Writer: Example: ₹10,000 at 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 2 years: 1.05^4 = 1.21550625, A = ₹12,155.06, CI = ₹2,155.06; effective rate 1.05^2 − 1 = 10.25%. Both examiner fixes applied (girl line and the recap board).

Checker: Line 3 (girl): 'So money grows faster every period?' is never answered, so it may suggest the rate itself rises. Correct version, e.g. teacher: 'The rate stays 10%, but the interest in rupees grows each period because the base is bigger.'
Checker: Line 10 board shows ₹12,155 but Line 12 says ₹12,155.06 (exact value 10,000 × 1.21550625 = ₹12,155.0625). Correct version: show ≈ ₹12,155.06 on the board so the two figures match.
Checker: Line 14: the effective rate doesn't say which case it uses. Correct version: 'For 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly: E = (1.05)² − 1 = 10.25% per annum.'
